def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if name not in KNOB_NAMES}
    env.update(overrides)
    return env


def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    import re

    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():
        for value in re.findall(rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
            matched = True
            total += float(value) * factor
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if name not in KNOB_NAMES}

def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    import re

    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():
        for value in re.findall(rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
            matched = True
            total += float(value) * factor
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if name not in KNOB_NAMES}

def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    import re

    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():
        for value in re.findall(rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
            matched = True
            total += float(value) * factor
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if name not in KNOB_NAMES}
    env.update(overrides)
    return env


def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    import re

    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():
        for value in re.findall(rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
            matched = True
            total += float(value) * factor
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record

    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    import re

    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():
        for value in re.findall(rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
            matched = True
            total += float(value) * factor
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if name not in KNOB_NAMES}
    env.update(overrides)
    return env


def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    import re

    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():
        for value in re.findall(rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
            matched = True
            total += float(value) * factor
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if name not in KNOB_NAMES}
    env.update(overrides)
    return env


def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    import re

    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():
        for value in re.findall(rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
            matched = True
            total += float(value) * factor
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

Now I see the `_dart_duration_seconds` helper. The bug: `re.findall(rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body)` — with `name = "seconds"`, the pattern matches inside `milliseconds`. Since factors dict is iterated insertion order: `milliseconds` first (0.001), then `seconds` (1.0) — so `Duration(milliseconds: 3000)` would be counted as 3.0 (from milliseconds factor) PLUS 3000.0 (from seconds substring match) = 3003.0. Exactly as the review says.

`_abortRunOrCompaction` → `_agent.abort()`. Let me check the agent abort path — what events fire when a stream is gated but abort is requested. Does the agent loop synthesize an aborted turn (AgentEndEvent) immediately?

{"command":"grep -n \"void abort\\|Future<void> abort\" lib/src/agent/agent.dart lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart | head; echo \"===\"; sed -n '/void abort()/,/^  }/p' lib/src/agent/agent.dart | head -25"}

The abort path: `_agent.abort()` cancels the active run's source. In the loop, when cancelled mid-stream, `_finishWithoutStream` fires with StopReason.aborted — emitting MessageStart/End events and then `AgentEndEvent`. The `streamHeartbeatProgress` classification stops the heartbeat on `MessageEndEvent/TurnEndEvent/AgentEndEvent`. So after an abort, the heartbeat is disarmed and ticks are silent.

For the E4 test, `GatedThinkingStreamFunction` ignores the cancelToken — its stream stays gated. But `_agent.abort()` → `_activeRun?.source.cancel()` — the agent loop listens for cancel during the stream... does it wait for the stream to end? Let me check how cancellation interacts with the gated stream. Look at the loop around line 1490-1520.

+    otherwise `Duration(milliseconds: 3000)` double-counts (3.0s from

+    a no-op refactor reds the one REG whose job is to be trusted.

+    def test_seconds_and_minutes_compose(self):
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(seconds: 300)"), 300.0)
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(minutes: 5)"), 300.0)

+class DartDurationParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Unit table for _dart_duration_seconds (gh-1430 review thread 1).
+
+    The coupling REG feeds this helper the `providerStreamIdleTimeout`
+    line straight from the Dart source, and the docstring promises the
+    parse survives a benign unit change there. `seconds` occurs INSIDE
+    `milliseconds`, so the unit match must be word-boundary anchored —
+    otherwise `Duration(milliseconds: 3000)` double-counts (3.0s from
+    the milliseconds factor + 3000.0s from the `seconds` substring) and
+    a no-op refactor reds the one REG whose job is to be trusted.
+    """
+
+    def test_seconds_and_minutes_compose(self):
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(seconds: 300)"), 300.0)
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(minutes: 5)"), 300.0)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)"), 90.0
+        )
+
+    def test_milliseconds_does_not_double_count_as_seconds(self):
+        # The exact case the substring matcher got wrong: `seconds`
+        # matched inside `milli**seconds**` → 3003.0 instead of 3.0.
+        self.assertEqual(

+        )

+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(milliseconds: 500)"), 0.5

+        )

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    def populate_context_post_run(self, context: AgentContext) -> None:
        """Fold fa's session token accounting into the agent context (issue #1123).

        fa session JSONL assistant records embed

        (Usage.toJson in lib/src/types.dart); summed across records this is

        adapter (bench/fa_usage.py): rglob covers retries and subagent
        sessions (E1/E2), records with omitted usage contribute a chars/4
        estimate tallied in context.metadata, and a missing/corrupt log

        Harbor semantics: n_input_tokens INCLUDES cache tokens. cost_usd
        comes from the pinned bench price table (bench/pricing.json);
        unpriced model → None, which the summary renders as n/a.
        """
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(self.logs_dir / "fah-sessions")

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    def populate_context_post_run(self, context: AgentContext) -> None:
        """Fold fa's session token accounting into the agent context (issue #1123).

        fa session JSONL assistant records embed
        ``message.usage = {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, ...}``
        (Usage.toJson in lib/src/types.dart); summed across records this is
        the billed usage for the trial. Extraction is shared with the legacy
        adapter (bench/fa_usage.py): rglob covers retries and subagent
        sessions (E1/E2), records with omitted usage contribute a chars/4
        estimate tallied in context.metadata, and a missing/corrupt log
        leaves zeros + a warning.

        Harbor semantics: n_input_tokens INCLUDES cache tokens. cost_usd
        comes from the pinned bench price table (bench/pricing.json);
        unpriced model → None, which the summary renders as n/a.
        """
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(self.logs_dir / "fah-sessions")

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    def populate_context_post_run(self, context: AgentContext) -> None:

        the billed usage for the trial. Extraction is shared with the legacy
        adapter (bench/fa_usage.py): rglob covers retries and subagent
        sessions (E1/E2), records with omitted usage contribute a chars/4
        estimate tallied in context.metadata, and a missing/corrupt log
        leaves zeros + a warning.

        Harbor semantics: n_input_tokens INCLUDES cache tokens. cost_usd
        comes from the pinned bench price table (bench/pricing.json);
        unpriced model → None, which the summary renders as n/a.
        """
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(self.logs_dir / "fah-sessions")

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

+class DartDurationParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Unit table for _dart_duration_seconds (gh-1430 review thread 1).
+
+    The coupling REG feeds this helper the `providerStreamIdleTimeout`
+    line straight from the Dart source, and the docstring promises the
+    parse survives a benign unit change there. `seconds` occurs INSIDE
+    `milliseconds`, so the unit match must be word-boundary anchored —
+    otherwise `Duration(milliseconds: 3000)` double-counts (3.0s from
+    the milliseconds factor + 3000.0s from the `seconds` substring) and
+    a no-op refactor reds the one REG whose job is to be trusted.
+    """
+
+    def test_seconds_and_minutes_compose(self):
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(seconds: 300)"), 300.0)
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(minutes: 5)"), 300.0)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)"), 90.0
+        )
+
+    def test_milliseconds_does_not_double_count_as_seconds(self):
+        # The exact case the substring matcher got wrong: `seconds`
+        # matched inside `milli**seconds**` → 3003.0 instead of 3.0.
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(milliseconds: 3000)"), 3.0
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(milliseconds: 500)"), 0.5
+        )
+
+    def test_mixed_milliseconds_and_seconds(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds(
+                "Duration(seconds: 3, milliseconds: 500)"
+            ),
+            3.5,
+        )
+
+    def test_no_duration_arguments_fails_loud(self):
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration()")
+

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

+class DartDurationParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Unit table for _dart_duration_seconds (gh-1430 review thread 1).
+
+    The coupling REG feeds this helper the `providerStreamIdleTimeout`
+    line straight from the Dart source, and the docstring promises the
+    parse survives a benign unit change there. `seconds` occurs INSIDE
+    `milliseconds`, so the unit match must be word-boundary anchored —
+    otherwise `Duration(milliseconds: 3000)` double-counts (3.0s from
+    the milliseconds factor + 3000.0s from the `seconds` substring) and
+    a no-op refactor reds the one REG whose job is to be trusted.
+    """
+
+    def test_seconds_and_minutes_compose(self):
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(seconds: 300)"), 300.0)
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(minutes: 5)"), 300.0)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)"), 90.0
+        )
+
+    def test_milliseconds_does_not_double_count_as_seconds(self):
+        # The exact case the substring matcher got wrong: `seconds`
+        # matched inside `milli**seconds**` → 3003.0 instead of 3.0.
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(milliseconds: 3000)"), 3.0
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(milliseconds: 500)"), 0.5
+        )
+
+    def test_mixed_milliseconds_and_seconds(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds(
+                "Duration(seconds: 3, milliseconds: 500)"
+            ),
+            3.5,
+        )
+
+    def test_no_duration_arguments_fails_loud(self):
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration()")
+
+

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    def populate_context_post_run(self, context: AgentContext) -> None:
        """Fold fa's session token accounting into the agent context (issue #1123).

        fa session JSONL assistant records embed
        ``message.usage = {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, ...}``
        (Usage.toJson in lib/src/types.dart); summed across records this is
        the billed usage for the trial. Extraction is shared with the legacy
        adapter (bench/fa_usage.py): rglob covers retries and subagent
        sessions (E1/E2), records with omitted usage contribute a chars/4
        estimate tallied in context.metadata, and a missing/corrupt log

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    def populate_context_post_run(self, context: AgentContext) -> None:
        """Fold fa's session token accounting into the agent context (issue #1123).

        fa session JSONL assistant records embed
        ``message.usage = {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, ...}``
        (Usage.toJson in lib/src/types.dart); summed across records this is
        the billed usage for the trial. Extraction is shared with the legacy
        adapter (bench/fa_usage.py): rglob covers retries and subagent
        sessions (E1/E2), records with omitted usage contribute a chars/4
        estimate tallied in context.metadata, and a missing/corrupt log
        leaves zeros + a warning.

        Harbor semantics: n_input_tokens INCLUDES cache tokens. cost_usd
        comes from the pinned bench price table (bench/pricing.json);
        unpriced model → None, which the summary renders as n/a.
        """
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(self.logs_dir / "fah-sessions")

+class DartDurationParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Unit table for _dart_duration_seconds (gh-1430 review thread 1).
+
+    The coupling REG feeds this helper the `providerStreamIdleTimeout`
+    line straight from the Dart source, and the docstring promises the
+    parse survives a benign unit change there. `seconds` occurs INSIDE
+    `milliseconds`, so the unit match must be word-boundary anchored —
+    otherwise `Duration(milliseconds: 3000)` double-counts (3.0s from
+    the milliseconds factor + 3000.0s from the `seconds` substring) and
+    a no-op refactor reds the one REG whose job is to be trusted.
+    """
+
+    def test_seconds_and_minutes_compose(self):
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(seconds: 300)"), 300.0)
+        self.assertEqual(_dart_duration_seconds("Duration(minutes: 5)"), 300.0)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)"), 90.0
+        )
+
+    def test_milliseconds_does_not_double_count_as_seconds(self):
+        # The exact case the substring matcher got wrong: `seconds`
+        # matched inside `milli**seconds**` → 3003.0 instead of 3.0.
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(milliseconds: 3000)"), 3.0
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration(milliseconds: 500)"), 0.5
+        )
+
+    def test_mixed_milliseconds_and_seconds(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dart_duration_seconds(
+                "Duration(seconds: 3, milliseconds: 500)"
+            ),
+            3.5,
+        )
+
+    def test_no_duration_arguments_fails_loud(self):
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            _dart_duration_seconds("Duration()")
+
+

+    def test_reasoning_heartbeat_lines_count_as_liveness_bytes(self):
+        # gh-1430: the `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` heartbeat is fa's
+        # in-band liveness signal alongside the ⏳ tool-liveness family —
+        # the #1185 AC6 audit disclosure must see BOTH, or a trial kept

+        # progress with zero disclosed liveness bytes.
+        heartbeat = "… reasoning 60s (streaming)\n"

+            fa_agent_timeout.liveness_bytes_of(heartbeat),
+            len("… reasoning 60s (streaming)".encode("utf-8")) + 1,
+        )
+        tier2 = "… reasoning 45s\n"
+        self.assertEqual(
+            fa_agent_timeout.liveness_bytes_of(tier2),
+            len("… reasoning 45s".encode("utf-8")) + 1,
+        )
+
+    def test_mixed_liveness_families_both_count(self):
+        stream = (
+            "assistant text\n"
+            "⏳ [bash] sleep 500 — running 60s\n"
+            "✓ bash · 61s\n"
+            "… reasoning 120s (streaming)\n"
+        )
+        measured = fa_agent_timeout.liveness_bytes_of(stream)

+            len(line.encode("utf-8")) + 1

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

+    def test_reasoning_heartbeat_lines_count_as_liveness_bytes(self):
+        # gh-1430: the `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` heartbeat is fa's
+        # in-band liveness signal alongside the ⏳ tool-liveness family —
+        # the #1185 AC6 audit disclosure must see BOTH, or a trial kept
+        # alive purely by reasoning heartbeats reports pane growth as
+        # progress with zero disclosed liveness bytes.
+        heartbeat = "… reasoning 60s (streaming)\n"
+        self.assertEqual(
+            fa_agent_timeout.liveness_bytes_of(heartbeat),
+            len("… reasoning 60s (streaming)".encode("utf-8")) + 1,
+        )
+        tier2 = "… reasoning 45s\n"
+        self.assertEqual(
+            fa_agent_timeout.liveness_bytes_of(tier2),
+            len("… reasoning 45s".encode("utf-8")) + 1,
+        )
+
+    def test_mixed_liveness_families_both_count(self):
+        stream = (
+            "assistant text\n"
+            "⏳ [bash] sleep 500 — running 60s\n"
+            "✓ bash · 61s\n"
+            "… reasoning 120s (streaming)\n"
+        )
+        measured = fa_agent_timeout.liveness_bytes_of(stream)
+        expected = sum(
+            len(line.encode("utf-8")) + 1
+            for line in stream.split("\n")
+            if "⏳" in line or "… reasoning" in line
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(measured, expected)
+        self.assertGreater(measured, 0)
+
+    def test_plain_reasoning_prose_is_not_a_liveness_line(self):
+        # The anchor is the ellipsis-led line head, not any mention of
+        # reasoning: assistant prose stays outside the disclosure.
+        self.assertEqual(
+            fa_agent_timeout.liveness_bytes_of("I reason therefore I am\n"),
+            0,
+        )

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    def populate_context_post_run(self, context: AgentContext) -> None:
        """Fold fa's session token accounting into the agent context (issue #1123).

        fa session JSONL assistant records embed
        ``message.usage = {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, ...}``
        (Usage.toJson in lib/src/types.dart); summed across records this is
        the billed usage for the trial. Extraction is shared with the legacy
        adapter (bench/fa_usage.py): rglob covers retries and subagent
        sessions (E1/E2), records with omitted usage contribute a chars/4
        estimate tallied in context.metadata, and a missing/corrupt log
        leaves zeros + a warning.

        Harbor semantics: n_input_tokens INCLUDES cache tokens. cost_usd
        comes from the pinned bench price table (bench/pricing.json);
        unpriced model → None, which the summary renders as n/a.
        """
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(self.logs_dir / "fah-sessions")

AssertionError: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0' not found in 'name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ inputs.model }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The optional self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot
      # write the hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the
      # runner's own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14.
      # The uv-managed CPython 3.13 user-space install below works on BOTH
      # runner kinds (the ubuntu-latest default included); uv is also the
      # canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}'
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ inputs.model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [ -n "$FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI" ] || { echo '::error::FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY secret is not set'; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py); absent inputs stay byte-for-byte
          # today's run (REG-1). A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # Pinned --job-name: one jobs/<name>/ dir per shard, so the summary
          # job's downloads cannot collide on harbor's timestamped default.
          # The family label keys results per dataset version (fa-4.0-*
          # matches the historical 4.0 names exactly).
          .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
            -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
            --job-name "fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${{ matrix.kind }}-${{ matrix.i }}" -o jobs \
            "${args[@]}"

      - name: Upload harbor job (shard ${{ matrix.i }})
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: harbor-job-shard-${{ matrix.i }}
          path: jobs/

      - name: Upload to Harbor Hub
        if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for job_dir in jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          MODEL: ${{ inputs.model }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" jobs
'

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of the ⏳ lines inside it (grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -F '\u23f3' /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation

#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):

#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a

on:

        required: false

        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:

        required: false

        required: false
